items.physical_scope: Formal coefficientwise gauge fixing and local renormalization data for the adopted pure SU(2) Yang–Mills model; it constructs no continuum functional measure or continuum theory.
items.statement:
Use the adopted pure $SU(2)$ Yang–Mills model: $G=SU(2)$, $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(2)$, the selected smooth right-principal bundle sector has no matter fields, and the positive invariant form is $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ with $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$ for $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, extended bilinearly to the graded coefficient algebra. Work in a nonempty local trivialization chart of the selected bundle over oriented, time-oriented Minkowski space with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and coordinates $x^0=t$ in natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $\eta_{\mu\nu}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and define $\partial^\mu:=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu$. With the alternating wedge–Lie bracket fixed by the principal-curvature supplier, write $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$. The adopted Lorentzian gauge action is $S_0[A]=-(2g_{\rm YM}^2)^{-1}\int\kappa(F_A\wedge *F_A)$, with fixed positive dimensionless $g_{\rm YM}$. In the perturbative formulas $A_\mu$ has canonical engineering dimension $1$ and $g_{\rm YM}$ dimension $0$ in mass units; the ghost $c$ has dimension $0$, the antighost $\bar c$ and auxiliary field $b$ have dimension $2$, and the BRST differential has dimension $0$. Assign each antifield $\Phi^*$ engineering dimension $4-\dim\Phi$, so its product with the corresponding BRST variation has density dimension $4$ whenever that variation is nonzero. The model postulate supplies the physical units, bundle sector, action, and boundary conditions; the classical gauge-invariance result supplies invariance under the declared bundle gauge transformations. This definition does not prove either supplier.

In the chosen local trivialization write $D_\mu c=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$ and choose the linear covariant gauge condition $G(A)=\partial^\mu A_\mu=0$ with gauge parameter $\xi>0$. The nonminimal BRST variables are an odd antighost $\bar c$ of ghost number $-1$ and an even auxiliary field $b$ of ghost number $0$, with $s\bar c=b$ and $sb=0$. The gauge-fixing fermion and gauge-fixing contribution are

$$\Psi_\xi=\int d^4x\,\kappa(\bar c,\partial^\mu A_\mu+\tfrac{\xi}{2}b),\qquad S_{\rm gf}:=s\Psi_\xi.$$

Here $s$ is the odd BRST derivation on the finite-jet field algebra, extended to the nonminimal variables and their antifields using the specified BV convention. The gauge condition is a local perturbative choice; it does not assert a global slice or remove all gauge copies. A finite-dimensional regulated configuration space has an ordinary Faddeev–Popov Jacobian only when it supplies the finite-dimensional group action, gauge condition, and transverse slice data in the preceding finite-dimensional definition. Such a Jacobian is not a continuum functional determinant and does not define a continuum measure.

For the relative local complex used in this datum, the field coordinates are $A_\mu^a,c^a,\bar c^a,b^a$ and their canonical antifields $A^{*\mu}_a,c^*_a,\bar c^*_a,b^*_a$. Each antifield $\Phi^*$ has parity $|\Phi|+1$ modulo $2$ and ghost number $-1-\operatorname{gh}(\Phi)$. The extended coefficient algebra $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}(U)$ is $C^\infty(U)$ tensored with the graded-commutative polynomial algebra in all even field/antifield jet generators and the exterior algebra in all odd field/antifield jet generators; each element depends on finitely many jets. For every multi-index $I\in\mathbb N^4$, total derivatives satisfy $D_\mu f=\partial_\mu f$ and $D_\mu\Phi_I=\Phi_{I+e_\mu}$; the $D_\mu$ commute. Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,p}(U)$, $0\le p\le4$, be the finite sums of horizontal $p$-forms with coefficients in the ghost-number-$g$ part of this algebra, where the $dx^\mu$ anticommute under wedge product; set $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,-1}(U)=\{0\}$ and $d_H=dx^\mu D_\mu$.

A **formal perturbative renormalization datum** consists of the selected pure SU(2) classical BV action $\Gamma_0$, the above gauge-fixing choice, the dimensional-regularization prescription $D=4-2\epsilon$ with a fixed positive reference mass scale $\mu$, modified minimal subtraction ($\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$), and a local counterterm space $\mathcal C_{\leq d_*}$. Fix the coupling convention $g_D(\mu,\epsilon)=\mu^\epsilon g(\mu)$ and $g_B=\mu^\epsilon Z_g g(\mu)$, where $g(\mu)$ is dimensionless, $g(\mu)=g_{\rm YM}$ at the selected reference scale, and $Z_g=1+O(\lambda)$ is the formal coupling-renormalization factor. Thus $g_D$ and the bare coupling $g_B$ have mass dimension $\epsilon$. With the geometric connection $A$ of dimension $1$, the dimensionally continued gauge action has coefficient $1/g_D^2=\mu^{-2\epsilon}/g(\mu)^2$; its density has dimension $4-2\epsilon=D$. The four-dimensional engineering dimensions used for local counterterms below remain those of the $\epsilon\to0$ local complex. Use the unrescaled $\mu$ convention: subtraction removes the pole parts together with the associated $-\gamma_E+\log(4\pi)$ constants, whose one-loop combination is $\Delta_\epsilon=1/\epsilon-\gamma_E+\log(4\pi)$. Equivalently, $\bar\mu^2=4\pi e^{-\gamma_E}\mu^2$ absorbs these constants into the scale; these two scale conventions are not applied simultaneously. This specifies scheme data and asserts neither a value for $Z_g$ nor a running-coupling equation. In the adopted pure-gauge sector, dimensional regularization is taken to preserve BRST in the formal analytic continuation: the regulator introduces no BRST-breaking term in the regularized gauge-fixed action or its defining rules. This is an explicit regulator property of the selected prescription, not a conclusion of the Slavnov–Taylor theorem and not an automatic claim about other matter contents or regularization schemes. The QAP and local anomaly-cancellation assumptions below remain separate. Here $d_*$ is a finite engineering-dimension bound fixed by the selected power-counting prescription; $\mathcal C_{\leq d_*}$ consists of integrated Lorentz-scalar polynomials of ghost number zero and engineering dimension at most $d_*$ in $A,c,\bar c,b$, their antifields, and finitely many spacetime derivatives, represented by elements of $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{0,4}(U)$. The usual renormalizable four-dimensional Yang–Mills choice is $d_*=4$. With the canonical BV convention, the classical master functional is

$$\Gamma_0=S_0+\int_U d^4x\left(A^{*\mu}_a(D_\mu c)^a+\tfrac12c^*_a[c,c]^a-\bar c^*_ab\right),$$

where the nonminimal term is omitted if that pair is not included. Let $s=B_{\Gamma_0}=(\Gamma_0,\cdot)$ be the local evolutionary representative of the canonical BV antibracket with this master functional: on each field and antifield jet it is prolonged by $s(D_I\Phi)=D_I(s\Phi)$, and on a horizontal form $dx^{\mu_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{\mu_p}\wedge a$ it is extended by $s(dx^{\mu_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{\mu_p}\wedge a)=(-1)^p dx^{\mu_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{\mu_p}\wedge sa$, so $s d_H+d_Hs=0$. Its restriction to $A,c,\bar c,b$ is the transformations already specified. The shifted Jacobi identity for the canonical antibracket gives $s^2X=\tfrac12((\Gamma_0,\Gamma_0),X)=0$ for every element $X$ of the canonical domain; the jet prolongation then gives the differential on the full finite-jet complex. The datum is admissible only when $\Gamma_0$ satisfies the classical master equation and the chosen local BV functional domain has no nonzero central element of ghost number one. Its loop-counting variable $\lambda$ is formal and dimensionless; a formal effective action is a coefficient sequence $\Gamma(\lambda)=\Gamma_0+\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda^n\Gamma_n$ and no convergence at any nonzero $\lambda$ is asserted.

For a local BV functional $\Gamma$, define the Slavnov functional by $\mathfrak S(\Gamma):=\tfrac12(\Gamma,\Gamma)$ using the chosen odd antibracket, and define the linearized operator $B_{\Gamma_0}X:=(\Gamma_0,X)$. The datum has the **local QAP property** when, at each first order $n$ where the coefficientwise Slavnov identity fails, its defect has a finite-jet local four-form representative $\delta_n\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{1,4}(U)$ and a finite-jet local three-form $\rho_n\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{2,3}(U)$ satisfying

$$\mathfrak S(\Gamma^{(<n)})=\lambda^n\int_U\delta_n+O(\lambda^{n+1}),\qquad B_{\Gamma_0}\delta_n+d_H\rho_n=0.$$

This local representative and consistency condition are part of the QAP input; take $\delta_n$ to have engineering dimension at most $d_*$ and $\rho_n$ at most $d_*-1$. The definition does not prove the QAP. Define the extended relative local cohomology by

$$H_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,p}(s\mid d_H):=\frac{\{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,p}(U):\text{there is }b\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g+1,p-1}(U)\text{ with }sa+d_Hb=0\}}{\{sm+d_Hn:m\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g-1,p}(U),\ n\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,p-1}(U)\}}.$$

For the counterterm-relevant restriction, let $\mathcal L_{\leq d_*}^{g,p}$ be the subspace of $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,p}(U)$ consisting of Lorentz-covariant local horizontal forms whose coefficient engineering dimension is at most $d_*-4+p$. Here covariance means that under a simultaneous proper orthochronous Lorentz change of coordinates, fields, antifields and jet indices, the expression transforms as a horizontal $p$-form, with no fixed noncovariant background tensor; this is a local covariance requirement on charts and does not require $U$ to be Lorentz invariant. Antifields transform in the dual tensor representations needed to make the displayed master density a scalar. In degree four this says precisely that the density multiplying the oriented volume form is a Lorentz scalar. In degree three it includes the covariant current forms whose horizontal derivative is a scalar density. The four-dimensional weights count $D_\mu$ as dimension $1$ and $s$ as dimension $0$; they are coefficient weights, so no dimension is assigned to the displayed $dx^\mu$ for this bound. Put $\mathcal L^{g,-1}_{\leq d_*}=0$. The scalar classical master action and the tensorial total derivatives preserve covariance; their dimension rules give $s\mathcal L^{g,p}_{\leq d_*}\subseteq\mathcal L^{g+1,p}_{\leq d_*}$ and $d_H\mathcal L^{g,p}_{\leq d_*}\subseteq\mathcal L^{g,p+1}_{\leq d_*}$. Define the restricted quotient for $g=0,1$ by

$$H_{\mathrm{Lor},\leq d_*}^{g,4}(s\mid d_H):=\frac{\{a\in\mathcal L_{\leq d_*}^{g,4}:sa+d_Hb=0\text{ for some }b\in\mathcal L_{\leq d_*}^{g+1,3}\}}{\{sm+d_Hn:m\in\mathcal L_{\leq d_*}^{g-1,4},\ n\in\mathcal L_{\leq d_*}^{g,3}\}}.$$

Both representatives and equivalence primitives are restricted: $m$ has scalar top-form density of dimension at most $d_*$, and $n$ is a covariant current three-form of coefficient dimension at most $d_*-1$. This denominator is contained in the numerator, since for $a=sm+d_Hn$ the allowed witness $b=sn$ gives $sa+d_Hb=0$. This restricted cohomology is not asserted equal to a subspace of unrestricted cohomology, nor to the minimal-only cohomology. The counterterm quotient means the infinitesimally Slavnov-invariant part of $\mathcal C_{\leq d_*}$ modulo precisely these allowed trivial counterterms and currents. For this datum's QAP and anomaly-cancellation hypotheses, require $\delta_n\in\mathcal L^{1,4}_{\leq d_*}$, $\rho_n\in\mathcal L^{2,3}_{\leq d_*}$ and any restoring primitive $\Xi_n\in\mathcal L^{0,4}_{\leq d_*}$, $\Theta_n\in\mathcal L^{1,3}_{\leq d_*}$. These are restrictions on the supplied local data, not an assertion that an unrestricted primitive can be replaced by a covariant bounded one. A $d_H$-exact top form represents zero as a local functional only under the declared compact-support or boundary condition. The coefficientwise Slavnov–Taylor identity is $\mathfrak S(\Gamma(\lambda))=0$ as an equality of formal power series.

items.physical_scope: Formal coefficientwise Slavnov–Taylor identities for the adopted pure SU(2) Yang–Mills perturbation theory, conditional on the QAP and local anomaly exactness; no continuum measure, convergence, nonperturbative existence, or empirical prediction is asserted.
items.statement:
In the axiom base inherited from the adopted model, fix the classical pure $SU(2)$ Yang–Mills model on oriented, time-oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, its selected smooth right-principal bundle sector $P\to M$, no matter fields, invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and fixed $g_{\rm YM}>0$. Let $U\subset M$ be a nonempty local trivialization chart, use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, and use the right-action curvature convention $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$. The adopted local classical action density is $-\kappa(F_A\wedge *_\eta F_A)/(2g_{\rm YM}^2)$. The local gauge potential $A_\mu$ is even with ghost number $0$ and engineering dimension $1$; the odd ghost $c$ has ghost number $1$ and dimension $0$. Define $D_\mu c=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$ and the minimal BRST transformations $sA_\mu=D_\mu c$, $sc=-\tfrac12[c,c]$. When the nonminimal pair is included, let $\bar c$ be odd with ghost number $-1$ and dimension $2$, and $b$ even with ghost number $0$ and dimension $2$, with $s\bar c=b$ and $sb=0$. Antifields have the opposite field parity and ghost number $-1-\operatorname{gh}(\Phi)$, with engineering dimension $\dim\Phi^*=4-\dim\Phi$, so a nonzero $\Phi^*s\Phi$ has density dimension $4$. Use the extended finite-jet local BV/nonminimal horizontal complex of the Formal Perturbative Yang–Mills Renormalization Data definition: its generators are the jets of $A,c,\bar c,b$ and their antifields, $d_H=dx^\mu D_\mu$, and $s=B_{\Gamma_0}$ is the prolonged canonical BV differential, with $s^2=0$ and $sd_H+d_Hs=0$ on the stated domain.

Use the canonical BV antibracket and let the classical BV functional be the pure-gauge extension
$$\Gamma_0=S_0+\int_U d^4x\left(A^{*\mu}_a(D_\mu c)^a+\tfrac12c^*_a[c,c]^a-\bar c^*_ab\right),$$
where the nonminimal term is omitted if that pair is not included, and $S_0$ denotes the adopted classical action on the chosen domain. Assume $\Gamma_0$ is even, has ghost number zero, satisfies $\tfrac12(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_0)=0$, and the chosen local BV functional domain has no nonzero central element of ghost number one. The model postulate and its classical gauge-invariance theorem are explicit inputs fixing and interpreting $S_0$; neither is proved by this theorem.

Choose the local Lorenz gauge $\partial^\mu A_\mu=0$ with constant $\xi>0$, dimensional regularization $D=4-2\epsilon$ with fixed positive reference mass $\mu$, $g_D=\mu^\epsilon g(\mu)$, $g_B=\mu^\epsilon Z_g g(\mu)$, $g(\mu)=g_{\rm YM}$ at the chosen scale, and modified minimal subtraction in the unrescaled-$\mu$ convention, removing pole parts and their associated $-\gamma_E+\log(4\pi)$ constants, and a finite engineering-dimension bound $d_*$. The geometric-connection gauge-action coefficient in the continued rules is $\mu^{-2\epsilon}/g(\mu)^2$, while all local cochain bounds below use four-dimensional engineering dimensions. For this adopted pure-gauge sector, treat dimensional regularization as BRST preserving in the formal analytic continuation, in the sense specified in the preceding formal-data definition; this is a regulator property, not a consequence of this theorem. The allowed counterterms are integrated Lorentz-scalar finite-jet polynomials of ghost number zero and dimension at most $d_*$ in $A,c,\bar c,b$, their antifields, and their spacetime derivatives. The formal loop variable $\lambda$ is dimensionless; $\Gamma(\lambda)=\Gamma_0+\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda^n\Gamma_n$ is a formal coefficient sequence with no convergence at nonzero $\lambda$ asserted. Write $\Gamma^{(<n)}$ for a partial action whose coefficients below order $n$ already satisfy the Slavnov identity.

Assume the local quantum action principle (QAP): at each first failing order $n$ there are a local ghost-number-one four-form $\delta_n\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{1,4}(U)$ of engineering dimension at most $d_*$ and local ghost-number-two three-form $\rho_n\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{2,3}(U)$ of dimension at most $d_*-1$ such that
$$\mathfrak S(\Gamma^{(<n)})=\lambda^n\int_U\delta_n+O(\lambda^{n+1}),\qquad B_{\Gamma_0}\delta_n+d_H\rho_n=0,$$
where $\mathfrak S(\Gamma)=\tfrac12(\Gamma,\Gamma)$, $B_{\Gamma_0}X=(\Gamma_0,X)$, and $d_H=dx^\mu D_\mu$ is the horizontal differential on finite-jet local forms. Assume local anomaly cancellation in the explicit form of a supplied sequence of allowed ghost-number-zero four-forms $\Xi_n\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{0,4}(U)$ and ghost-number-one three-forms $\Theta_n\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{1,3}(U)$ satisfying
$$\delta_n=B_{\Gamma_0}\Xi_n+d_H\Theta_n$$
at every first failing order; put $\Xi_n=\Theta_n=0$ at nonfailing orders. Compact support or the model's boundary conditions make the integral of each $d_H$-exact four-form vanish. Then the counterterm series $C(\lambda)=-\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda^n\int_U\Xi_n$ yields $\mathfrak S(\Gamma(\lambda)+C(\lambda))=0$ coefficientwise.

Use the formal-data definition's Lorentz-covariant subspaces $\mathcal L_{\leq d_*}^{g,p}$ of the full BV/nonminimal complex: coefficients have dimension at most $d_*-4+p$, top forms have Lorentz-scalar densities, and three-forms are covariant currents. Assume the QAP representatives and supplied exactness sequence lie in these subspaces: $\delta_n\in\mathcal L^{1,4}_{\leq d_*}$, $\rho_n\in\mathcal L^{2,3}_{\leq d_*}$, $\Xi_n\in\mathcal L^{0,4}_{\leq d_*}$, and $\Theta_n\in\mathcal L^{1,3}_{\leq d_*}$. For $g\in\{0,1\}$ use $H_{\mathrm{Lor},\leq d_*}^{g,4}(s\mid d_H)$: its cocycles are $a\in\mathcal L^{g,4}_{\leq d_*}$ with $sa+d_Hb=0$ for some $b\in\mathcal L^{g+1,3}_{\leq d_*}$, and equivalences are $a\sim a+sm+d_Hn$ with $m\in\mathcal L^{g-1,4}_{\leq d_*}$ and $n\in\mathcal L^{g,3}_{\leq d_*}$. Thus both cochains and primitives obey covariance and the stated bounds; unrestricted BV exactness alone is insufficient. The resulting ghost-number-zero quotient is exactly the infinitesimally Slavnov-invariant local counterterm freedom modulo the stated allowed trivial counterterms and total derivatives. The ghost-number-one quotient classifies local obstruction classes in that space; a nonzero class cannot be removed by an allowed local counterterm. This is a quotient statement and asserts no finite basis of representatives. The conclusion is conditional on the local QAP and supplied anomaly-cancellation sequence; it proves neither premise and asserts no empirical result, continuum functional measure, convergence, or nonperturbative existence. Any finite-dimensional Faddeev–Popov Jacobian remains the ordinary Jacobian of its specified regulated group action and transverse slice; it is not a continuum functional determinant.

items.title: A Finite Orbit with Two Gauge-Condition Intersections
items.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional regulated gauge-orbit example only; it is not a non-Abelian Yang–Mills field theory or a continuum functional measure.
items.statement:
Let $X=\mathbb R^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$ have positive density $|dx\,dy|$, and let $K=S^1$ have angle coordinate $\theta$ and right-invariant density $|d\theta|$. Let $K$ act on the right by
$$(x,y)\cdot e^{i\theta}=(x\cos\theta-y\sin\theta,x\sin\theta+y\cos\theta).$$
For $r>0$, set $s_r=(r,0)$, choose an open neighborhood $U_r\subset\{x>0\}$ of $s_r$, let $S_r=U_r\cap\{y=0\}$ have density $|dx|$, and set $\chi(x,y)=y$ on $U_r$. The unit angular generator $1\in\mathfrak k=T_eK\cong\mathbb R$ has infinitesimal orbit vector
$$R_{s_r}(1):=\left.\frac{d}{d\theta}\right|_{0}(s_r\cdot e^{i\theta})=(0,r).$$
The Faddeev–Popov operator is the linear map $M_{s_r}:=d\chi_{s_r}\circ R_{s_r}:\mathfrak k\to\mathbb R$, and its density Jacobian relative to $|d\theta|$ and $|dy|$ is $\Delta_{\rm FP}(s_r)=|\det M_{s_r}|=r>0$. The full orbit $K\cdot s_r$ nevertheless meets the global condition $y=0$ at both $(r,0)$ and $(-r,0)$. Thus the local nonzero Jacobian proves transversality near $s_r$ but does not select one global representative for the orbit. The regulator group $K$ in this finite-dimensional toy is not identified with the model's non-Abelian structure group $G$.

items.physical_scope: A local formal Lorenz-gauge functional in the finite-jet Yang–Mills BRST algebra; no global slice, continuum measure, or empirical prediction is asserted.
items.statement:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ be a nonempty open region with compact support or boundary conditions that remove total-derivative terms. Use $\eta_{\mu\nu}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\partial^\mu:=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu$. Work in the adopted pure $SU(2)$ model, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and normalized positive $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, extended bilinearly to the graded coefficient algebra. In the finite-jet algebra take $A_\mu$ to be an even $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $0$ and dimension $1$, $c$ an odd $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $1$ and dimension $0$, $\bar c$ an odd $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $-1$ and dimension $2$, and $b$ an even $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $0$ and dimension $2$. Let $\xi>0$ be dimensionless. Use the Lie-algebra bracket and odd left BRST derivation

$$sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],\qquad sc=-\tfrac12[c,c],\qquad s\bar c=b,\qquad sb=0,$$

extended to jets by commuting with total derivatives. Define the Lorenz-gauge fermion and its BRST-exact functional by

$$\Psi_\xi=\int_U d^4x\,\kappa(\bar c,\partial^\mu A_\mu+\tfrac{\xi}{2}b),\qquad S_{\rm gf}:=s\Psi_\xi.$$

Then

$$S_{\rm gf}=\int_U d^4x\,\left(\kappa(b,\partial^\mu A_\mu)+\tfrac{\xi}{2}\kappa(b,b)-\kappa(\bar c,\partial^\mu D_\mu c)\right),\qquad D_\mu c:=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],$$

is a local, even, ghost-number-zero functional of density dimension $4$, and it is BRST-closed. It is an exact gauge-fixing term in the formal local algebra; this example does not claim a global representative for every gauge orbit or a continuum functional measure.
